correctness.rationale: The original increment-history process couples exactly to percolated random recursive trees. Conditional binary parity expectation is 1 precisely when every forest component has even size, otherwise 0. Increasing-tree decomposition by root-component parity proves A'=e^A sinh(alpha B), B'=e^A cosh(alpha B), with unique formal coefficients and q_n=n[z^n]A. The change u=tanh(B/3) gives z=3u-u^3 at alpha=1/3, and Lagrange inversion yields the binomial sum. A negative-binomial CLT with mean m and variance 3m/2 proves the leading (3/4)4^{-m} TV constant. Standalone exact-rational code independently matches 60 coefficients with forest recursions and 30 cases with direct increment-history enumeration.

value.rationale: The smallest nontrivial finite-group example used to demonstrate nonmonotone reinforced mixing acquires a complete exact finite-time mixing profile, a general computable generating-function representation and a sharp decay constant at the first nontrivial polynomial-integrability parameter alpha=1/3. This distinguishes infinitely many exactly uniform odd times from exponentially small but strictly positive even-time defects and quantifies both exponent and prefactor beyond the available broad exponential bounds. The cubic parameter is structurally motivated by polynomial inversion, not an arbitrary numerical slice.
